content.title: What's it like for UCLA's Sienna Betts to play with her sister Lauren? We asked her
content.text: April 3, 2026, 6:37 a.m. ETSisters Lauren and Sienna Betts are teammates on the UCLA women's basketball team.Sienna initially did not want to play with her older sister in college to forge her own path.The sisters have learned to give each other space, improving their on and off-court relationship.Lauren is a projected top-five WNBA draft pick, and Sienna is expected to take on a larger role next season.When UCLA freshman Sienna Betts made a mistake in practice early this season, she heard her sister Lauren, a senior, yelling at her. Sienna’s first thought was a common one for younger siblings. “Please shut up.”“She's a leader,” Sienna said of Lauren, who is projected to be a top-five pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. “It's a hard boundary because, if I'm mad at myself, I don't want to listen to my sibling. And I'm like, ‘Let me just listen to the coaches.’”As Lauren, 22, and Sienna, 19, prepare for the Bruins’ Final Four matchup against Texas on April 3, they’re used to seeing the “typical” sister stories about having their built-in best friend on the court. Watch Final Four on FuboBut when Lauren decided to make the jump to UCLA from Stanford in 2023, Sienna, then a high school sophomore, wasn’t thrilled about it.“I wasn't gonna come here anymore,” said Sienna, who had UCLA as her top college choice at the time. “I didn't want to. I didn't want to hear, ‘I came here for my sister,’ and I didn't want to play college with her just because we've butted heads so much growing up.”This line of thinking was nothing new for Sienna. She has always been her own person.“Sienna really likes to have the opportunity to do things on her own and have things to herself,” said Michelle Betts, the sisters’ mother. “And so, she would have liked to have had UCLA to herself.”It took months for Sienna to even make the decision to go to UCLA after Lauren announced her move. Her family became a non-factor in her college choice.“I think at that time she kind of wanted to figure things out on her own,” Michelle said. “After Lauren went to UCLA, it seemed like Sienna didn't really want us as involved in her recruiting as we had been.”According to some reports, Sienna was swayed toward UCLA with a PowerPoint that her sister made on the day she verbally committed. Sienna quickly dispelled that notion.“That day I was already planning on committing,” Sienna said. “So it wasn't like it was a deciding factor. Everyone keeps saying that.”Growing up, the sibling rift was always present. Off the court, it’s no more than your run-of-the-mill sister drama. On the court, the clash of personalities takes a bit of a different shape.This season isn’t the first time that the Betts sisters have played on the same team. They played together as a freshman and a senior in high school in Aurora, Colorado.“It was pretty different from this year,” Sienna said. “I mean, I was a starter, but also I think our relationship wasn't as good. We were around each other so much, and we were just forced to be around each other so much, like living together.”Sienna said she worried that playing with her sister again would mean more of the same conflicts as that year in high school. At Sienna’s request, Lauren has left the mentoring of her younger sister to the coaches and her fellow seniors like Angela Dugalic and Charlisse Leger-Walker.Lauren also made sure to make Sienna feel welcome from the first day at UCLA, but she had to know her boundaries with her younger sister.“Lauren was really good at introducing me to everyone and being there for me and helping me through all of that, but also giving me my space to go through it by myself,” Sienna said. “That was a really big thing for me. I wanted to figure out my freshman year by myself, and not have someone there defending me like an older sister.”This new dynamic between the Betts sisters has brought them closer. Their mother was shocked when they came home for Christmas and optionally chose to hang out together.“I was like, ‘Gosh, they're going to the mall together?’” Michelle said. “That was really nice to see.”Even as their relationship has grown this season, all of the Betts are excited for a time when the sisters aren’t on the same team. Lauren is poised to have a promising future in the WNBA, while Sienna, who has averaged 14.7 minutes off the bench this season, will get a chance to step into the limelight next season.“I think she's going to be huge for next year,” Lauren said. “And she's going to continue to work hard and take this team really far. She hasn't played as much, obviously, as she wants to play this year, but that doesn't take away from her talent and how amazing she's going to be for this program.”Michelle said she looks forward to Sienna and Lauren forging their own paths again.“I'm actually really excited for them to be able to do their own thing again,” Michelle said. “Especially Sienna. I'm excited for her to be back where she was looking forward to being.”Where to watch Texas vs. UCLA in Final FourTV: ESPNStreaming: Fubo | SlingWhat time is Texas vs. UCLA game?Tip-off: 9:30 p.m. ET on April 3Jack Little is a student in the University of Georgia’s Carmical Sports Media Institute.
